speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this painful ulcer on your leg started, and how long has it been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the painful nature of the ulcer, I need to rule out pyoderma gangrenosum. Do you have any other skin lesions, and have you noticed if the ulcer edges are violaceous or undermined?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of an ant bite at the site and the presence of dilated tortuous veins, this may be a traumatic ulcer with secondary infection or stasis dermatitis rather than pyoderma gangrenosum. I will order a wound culture and a lower extremity venous Doppler to evaluate for venous insufficiency and rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture; REQUEST TEST: Lower_Extremity_Venous_Doppler

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional systemic symptoms mentioned. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of painful ulcers with violaceous borders, a history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, and the onset following minor trauma (ant bite) is classic for Pyoderma Gangrenosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
